text:
alex_support: FYI customer 'NovaPay' reporting big p99 spikes on Dedicated yesterday evening, their SLAs hit. They say API generation p99 climbed from ~400ms to ~4.2s across multiple routes.
meera_sre: ok moving to eng-sre. do we have correlation with any scale events or provisioning errors around 19:12 UTC? link to their case: https://redwood.internal/cases/CP-4421
josh_runtime: I pulled the pool logs for their dedicated pool id dp-34. There's a cluster of attach-timeouts and GPU init stalls around 19:10-19:25. cpu/mem not maxed but attach queue length spiked.
meera_sre: paste of relevant snippet:
```
2026-03-12T19:11:04Z attach-request from router trace=abc123 pool=dp-34
2026-03-12T19:11:04Z pending-attach queue_size=32
2026-03-12T19:11:08Z gpu-init start instance=i-0a1b2c
2026-03-12T19:11:21Z gpu-init complete instance=i-0a1b2c duration_ms=17123
2026-03-12T19:11:22Z attach success instance=i-0a1b2c
```
meera_sre: gpu-init duration of ~17s is the red flag — that's a cold GPU start cost. customer traffic pattern had a short spike which pushed the autoscaler to request new instances, and we hit the slow path.
ryan_platform: any errors from the provisioner? I see throttles on our provisioning API around that time due to a brief control-plane rate limiter bump (we were rotating a couple of nodes for maintenance). That might've delayed handoff.
josh_runtime: also saw a few fallback events where requests were rerouted from dp-34 to hosted fallback model variant (lower perf). That explains the larger p99 for user-facing requests.
alex_support: customer noticed consistent p99 regressions even after steady traffic — said it persisted for ~20 minutes.
meera_sre: ok breakdown: two contributors: (1) scale-up lag (provisioner throttle + slow GPU init) (2) pool saturation + queueing leading to some requests hitting fallback path.
josh_runtime: digging into runtime metrics: attach latency distribution shows bi-modal behavior. warm attaches ~150ms, cold attaches >10s. prefix-cache misses also higher for those cold instances causing extra model load time.
meera_sre: actions we tried in-thread: bumped dp-34 min_capacity from 2 -> 4 for emergency, temporarily increased attach-timeout threshold to avoid early re-routes, and toggled aggressive prewarm for that customer. monitored for 15min and p99 dropped back to ~600ms.
alex_support: customer accepted the temporary mitigation but wants root cause and permanent fix. They flagged this as Sev-2.
ryan_platform: follow-ups: (a) increase default prewarm window for Dedicated pools that have high burstiness, (b) add graceful backoff in provisioner instead of hard throttle, (c) expose pool attach queue metric to console for customers.
josh_runtime: we should also optimize gpu-init path — current container startup includes loading weight shards from S3 which is taking time when instance is cold. propose: (1) allow lazy model mmap and async weight streaming for large models, (2) keep a small pool of prewarmed idle replicas per busy customer.
meera_sre: short-term runbook updates I will make today: detect attach-duration > 5s alert, auto-increase min_capacity for 10m for affected pool, and notify oncall with suggested customer-facing message.
meera_sre: sample alert rule:
```
alert: DedicatedAttachLatencyHigh
expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(attach_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, pool)) > 5
for: 2m
```
josh_runtime: repro steps if you want to simulate locally:
1) create a dedicated pool with min_capacity=0, scale_to=8, model=large-15b, sequence_length=2048
2) hammer traffic with 200 qps for 2 minutes then drop to 5 qps
3) watch attach queue and provisioning events

alex_support: I left a customer note: "We're rolling an emergency scaling change and investigating root cause; expect follow-up with timeline." they asked for ETA on permanent fix.
ryan_platform: ETA rough: low-lift fixes (prewarm window + runbook) within 48h. Provisioner backoff + console metric ~1 week. GPU-init work depends on runtime team prioritization, estimate 3-5 weeks.
josh_runtime: will open a tracking PR for async weight streaming and a small experiment to keep 1-2 prewarmed replicas per customer — linking after I create it.
meera_sre: I'm creating an internal postmortem ticket and will attach traces/dashboard snapshots. assigning owners: meera -> runbook + alerts ; ryan -> provisioner backoff + console metrics ; josh -> runtime gpu-init optimization + PR ; alex -> customer comms + follow-ups.
sre-oncall-bot: Incident CP-4421 assigned: sev=2, owner=meera_sre, sla=48h
deploy-bot: noted that there was a maintenance rotation job at 19:08 UTC which may have contributed to control-plane load.
meera_sre: final note for now — recommended customer mitigation we offered: pin to a dedicated-mini pool (min_capacity=2, prewarm=true) or enable fallback-less routing for critical routes so requests won't be rerouted to hosted models during attach storms. Customer will decide.
alex_support: customer will accept the dedicated-mini option for now and requested a short FAQ on why p99 jumps — i'll draft and share.
meera_sre: thanks all. i'll upload the raw logs + dashboard links to the ticket. follow up in the postmortem thread once we have PRs and timelines.
alex_support: marking this thread as resolved for the customer comms for now. will reopen if anything else pops up. :white_check_mark:
